The best way to fight these attacks on voting and elections is by registering as many new voters as we can and getting them to vote in November.
Our program costs $3 per new voter. Join the movement with $30 or more right now to register new voters and more >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=080226_3&amount=30]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Voter registration is a core part of how we fight back against suppression, folks.
How do we do it? We maximize your impact by focusing on the underserved and ignored portions of eligible voters. The unregistered, eligible citizens. Previous voters who let their registration lapse. Anyone who feels disregarded and disconnected from the political process.
Why them? Candidates and their political campaigns target those most likely to turn out. They hyper-focus on "persuadables" and "reliable partisans." Rather than trying to compete with their resources, we maximize your impact by speaking directly to Americans who feel left behind as they lose their fundamental rights.
We drive these eligible citizens to participation by helping them understand the stakes and showing how their vote matters . That's why our voter registration efforts are so important: Everyone should vote and feel invested in the outcome.
Just $3 can help us register a new voter. Will you step up with $30 or more today to help register 10 new voters? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=080226_3&amount=30]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?express_lane=true&refcode=080226_3&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?express_lane=true&refcode=080226_3&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?express_lane=true&refcode=080226_3&amount=50]

Unfortunately, we don't have anywhere near the resources to blanket the country with our efforts. Each election cycle, we target specific states where our efforts will make the greatest difference, like Nevada, North Carolina, or Michigan.
The key is getting these disenfranchised people -- always the first target of opponents of voting rights across the country -- to see the importance of voting now more than ever.
Voting quickly becomes a habit -- a habit our democracy sorely needs to fulfill the promise of the American dream. Overwhelming key states with new voter registrations can help turn the tide against the voter suppression laws we've seen passed over the last few years.
New voter registration -- at a cost to us of just about $3 per new voter -- is the whole ballgame. Can you pitch in with $30 or however much you can to help us register new voters ahead of registration deadlines? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=080226_3&amount=30]

Voter Action Project's Registration Team

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

Peter, the stakes

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260802-2.AmUIbM&refcode=em20260802-38120&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=38120%2E1203867%2Eehkne6 ]Rush a grassroots contribution now to help us win all three →

We have Cori Bush in the race to reclaim MO-01 from AIPAC stooge Wesley
Bell, Donavan McKinney challenging multimillionaire Shri Thanedar in
MI-13, and Justin J. Pearson stepping up to fight GOP fascism in TN-09.

Every one of these races is a fight we cannot afford to lose, and another
prime opportunity to build our bloc in Congress.

All three candidates are ready to give their districts a Democratic
representative who actually shows up for working people — not one who
sells out to corporate PACs, the pro-Israel lobby, or the establishment.

We've had a strong primary season already with 8 Justice Democrats winning
their primaries or advancing to the general this year. But if we win these
next three, we can potentially elect almost a DOZEN new progressives to
strengthen our fight for Medicare for All, an end to genocide and forever

subject: Concerning the August 4 Election Night Party Controversy

body:
Come join us on August 4 for our election watch party! The drinks and snacks may be free, but freedom? That's never free.

| | | | | |
---
| | | | | |
Hey, all!
Adam here again. Don’t worry, there’s still no controversy. Just tricking you into opening my emails again. I regret nothing.
The big news for today: Election day is Tuesday, August 4th. Go vote before 7pm, then make sure you come to our big party in Arlington to watch the results roll in. We also have an art contest! It’s fun, you should submit something. Our campaign manager Jake insisted on this art contest idea, and if you don’t submit something to his contest, it’ll break his fragile little heart.
He’s a sensitive boy, don’t hurt him.
Details below. See y’all Tuesday!
\- Adam
**WATCH PARTY** We’ve got details and tickets available for our [August 4th Election Day party](https://us.list-manage.com/CVN7LOmmruE?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0). Tickets are free, nothing snooty. Casual dress code, come as you are. 7:30 PM at Courthaus Social in Arlington, VA.
Everyone and anyone is invited to attend, so if you’re in vicinity of Northern Virginia on Tuesday, come through. And, as modern air travel became accessible in the mid-20th century, there’s really no excuse for anyone on planet earth to _not_ be in the vicinity of Northern Virginia by Tuesday. So I guess I’ll see you Tuesday.
And before anybody asks, “oh but _Adam_ , what about _me_ , I’m an astronaut on the International Space Station, I’m not on earth. Am _I_ allowed to miss the party?” Dumb question. Gravity is free and it goes straight down. So you guys have even less excuse. You’re astronauts. I thought you were supposed to be smart.

**ART CONTEST** Thanks to everyone so far who has submitted their entries for our art contest. For those of you who haven’t seen yet, Eddie the Edgy Eagle has a simple question:

Here are some submissions so far!This was sent in from a very special supporter. He loves video games and baseball and race cars. And we love him.

This was drawn by a practicing attorney from Norfolk, Virginia. So, you know, careful who you call for help down in Norfolk.
Send in an illustration of your answer to Eddie’s question “DO U LIKE DEMOCRACY” by lunchtime tomorrow and our panel of judges (me) will post the winners (my favorites). Submissions will be graded on 3 aspects: (1) Is it cool? (2) How fun is it? (3) Bravery.
“But aren’t those criteria very subjective? And ‘bravery’ doesn’t even make sense?” Oh, here we go with the astronaut questions again.
_-_ Adam
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/YqA61M9BME4?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0)
| | **Voter Guide Is Here!** We made a (mostly impartial) voter guide. I did my best to keep it factual, saved my personal thoughts and opinions toward the end. So, if you know anyone still making their mind up about August 4th, forward liberally. I was also slightly silly in this video. Lightly humorous. Modestly tomfoolish. So maybe that’ll make this boring political stuff a little more fun. Let me know what you think.
We also made a [fun video specifically for Republicans!](https://us.list-manage.com/13mLcRv6T_f?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0) So, send this around to your conservative friends who need to hear it. Especially if they live in Virginia’s 8th.
---
| | **Things to Know About August 4th** Voting on August 4th may be daunting if you’ve never voted in a primary, but we’re here to make it simple. Watch [the video above](https://us.list-manage.com/UvTmL7TZt8o?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0) for the long version, or if you just want the links and info, here they are:
**Where and When to Vote** If you’re already registered, [click here to find your polling place and hours](https://us.list-manage.com/14sGbwtVOTE?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0). Go vote, don’t procrastinate. On election day, remember: If you’re in line to vote, even after closing hours, they have to let you vote. So go participate in your democracy, and don’t take “no” for an answer.
**Not Registered to Vote? No Problem!**[Click here to make sure you’re registered](https://us.list-manage.com/Su0AyJD3TgU?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0), and if you’re not, [click here to find out how to register to vote.](https://us.list-manage.com/JgL4qzBQZuL?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0) Virginia lets you register and vote same-day in person at the polls, so there’s no excuse to sit this election out. Show up on August 4th, bring the required documents, and register/vote. DO THIS. GO VOTE. EVERYONE VOTE. Doesn’t have to be for me, just show up for your democracy right now, it’s important.
**Notice Any Tomfoolery on August 4th?** So, this is kind of important: Trump and the DOJ are sending “election observers” to locations across Virginia on August 4th. This may be nothing, but it’s possible that some of those observers may try to intimidate or interfere with polling operations on election day. If you see anything that feels off, make a report to the [Election Protection hotline](https://us.list-manage.com/1BgujtaC5kz?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0). No need to freak out, but vigilance is the price of democracy. So be vigilant.
---
| | **Media Appearances** Here’s our list of recent media appearances. My favorite was the Adam Kinzinger interview, but we did pretty well on WUSA9 too. At any rate, watch all of them. Comment, like, do all the social media things so the algorithm takes notice.
[Adam and Adam: Let’s get at ‘em (Kinzinger interview)](https://us.list-manage.com/byC8U45c3WD?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0)[WUSA9 and ABC7 Candidate Profiles](https://us.list-manage.com/18gFguCza01?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0)[Appearance on the Destiny Livestream](https://us.list-manage.com/f78ErNRldIj?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0)[Appearance on the David Clayton Stream](https://us.list-manage.com/15JGJAMKCCM?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0)[Educational Piece: How to Spot a CIA Plant](https://us.list-manage.com/v2LJOyR7kO_?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0) (VERY important, must watch)
---

How many times have you sat down to dinner with your family after a long day, only to be interrupted by an annoying robocall? Then another. Then another — each one leaving a voicemail and clogging up your inbox.
Everyone hates robocalls and the never-ending disruptions they bring into our lives. But these calls aren’t just annoying. In many cases, they’re illegal, and a vehicle for scams that can cause real financial harm for Americans .
So I joined a coalition of 49 attorneys general to continue our national, bipartisan fight to protect consumers from unwanted robocalls. Together, we submitted a comment letter in support of the FCC’s new proposed regulations that would ensure service providers know who they are providing service to.
If that’s all you need to hear, please click here to support my re-election campaign today so I can continue fighting to protect Californians. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
Tackling robocalls is not a new fight for my office. For years, we’ve been working to put a stop to these illegal calls and hold bad actors accountable:
We’ve sued Avid Telecom for allegedly initiating and facilitating billions of unlawful robocalls, including Social Security, Medicare, and employment scams. We’ve sent warning letters to telecom companies passing suspected illegal robocall traffic through their networks, including calls impersonating government officials. And we’ve sent comment letters to the FCC on the growing threat of AI-generated robocalls and how to strengthen existing rules to keep up.
The message we’re sending is clear: illegal robocalls will not be tolerated, and those responsible will be held accountable.
I’m running for re-election so I can continue this work — and so California never backs down from protecting consumers and enforcing the law.

subject: This is why I walked away
disclaimer_text: Paid for by VPP
body:
| I’m sure you’ve heard the news, team.

DNC Chair, Ken Martin, is busy throwing phones at staffers, forcing officers to sign NDAs in order to see the budget, and mortgaging the DNC’s headquarters just to keep the lights on.

One thing is clear: **The establishment is in complete disarray.**

When I was Vice Chair, I saw the writing on the wall. I saw firsthand that the establishment wasn’t willing to do what it takes to restore trust in our party and win. It’s why I walked away.

And now the absolute chaos inside the DNC is undeniable. _Even James Carville, who has not historically been my biggest fan, has suggested that I step in as chair and fix this mess._

**Let me be clear: we’re in a critical, must win election year.** This is the moment to be aggressively building grassroots infrastructure, mobilizing voters, and supporting leaders who will break the GOP’s grip on power and give us a real fighting chance in 2028.

**Instead, Ken Martin and the DNC are managing decline — to the tune of $18M in debt while Republicans outraise us 8 to 1.**

All of this coming on the heels of Ken Martin botching the 2024 election autopsy, failing to answer basic questions about why we lost to Trump _again_ and what we’re going to do about it (not to mention the fact that he left the entire “Conclusion” section blank!).

I’ve said it before and I’ll keep saying it: the solution to our party’s failure is _NOT_ going to come from inside this DNC.

These political insiders are trapped in a cycle of damage control and self preservation. If we want a movement that actually fights for working people, is capable of taking on Trump’s agenda, and winning — _we have to get in the dirt and do it ourselves._

**That’s exactly why Leaders We Deserve exists.** We do the work the establishment is refusing to do. We don’t protect the status quo. We back candidates who won’t hesitate to take on MAGA extremism and who actually have the guts to fight for the people not corporate special interests and give us hope for the future.

And we need you with us today to continue doing the work of electing a truly new generation of leaders that will return the Democratic party to a winning coalition in 2026 and beyond.

[While Ken Martin and the DNC manage crisis after crisis, we’re building the real long term power we need to reignite our party and win. That work is fueled by grassroots donations from emails like this. Peter, we're a 100% people-powered campaign. I’m the only candidate in this race who’s never taken corporate PAC money or AIPAC checks, and I never, ever will. That means when it comes to funding the organizing efforts that actually decides who wins this race, I'm counting on folks like you. So please, don’t bet on us. Invest in us. Congress is racing to expand military AI, cyber, and intelligence integration with a foreign government -- while an automatic draft registry comes online six weeks after you vote. **Adam Smith cosponsored the bill.** Then he went on a national podcast the day before the final vote and told people not to worry about it.
[Congressman Adam Smith](https://substack.com/redirect/af52b2bd-09af-4cae-9397-1cc1e4567d35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) _(historical top donor, AIPAC, top ~15, the military-surveillance-industrial complex)_ went on Breaking Points on July 21 and was asked, point blank, about Section 219 of the defense bill he cosponsored. (Formerly Section 224.) His answer: the Pentagon runs "literally thousands" of programs, and this is maybe three, four, five, six of them. Call it a merger, he said, and that's "an incredible exaggeration."
He wants you to count programs.
**I want you to ask what those programs do.**
A military can have thousands of programs -- radios, uniforms, spare parts, office software, belts and boot laces, toothpaste. **Section 219 is not that.** It concerns artificial intelligence, biotechnology, autonomous weapons, cyberwarfare, quantum computing, biological/chemical/nuclear weapons and the intelligence-fusion systems that will decide how future wars are fought and who in them lives or dies.
Six programs that monopolize those systems - the central nervous system of American military might for decades to come - are not the same as six hundred programs that supply boots, laces, and buttons.
Smith knows the difference. He's making fools out of us all, on purpose. He's spent nearly three decades on the Armed Services Committee and is its ranking Democrat when Republicans are in power - and the Chair of the whole committee when Democrats hold the Oval Office.
That's exactly why his numbers game deserves scrutiny, not a pass.
## What Section 219 Actually Does
Section 219 -- numbered 224 when it was first written, carried in the Senate's version of the NDAA as Section 1217 -- creates the **U.S.-Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative**. It orders the Secretary of Defense to name a permanent **" executive agent"** inside the Pentagon whose job is to "synchronize, expand, and accelerate" joint research, testing, and industrial cooperation with Israel's defense sector.
The covered domains, straight from the bill: artificial intelligence and autonomous systems, cyber and electronic warfare, quantum technology, biotechnology, directed energy weapons, missile and air defense, counter-drone systems, and data fusion -- plus a standing pathway for moving Israeli-origin (_meaning, they developed it on our dime and tested it by slaughtering innocents)_ or jointly developed technology into official U.S. weapons programs. That means, they'd have backdoor access to everything, lock, stock and barrel.
That is not a request to keep doing what we're already doing. It's an instruction to do more of it, faster, under one office explicitly located ABOVE the Pentagon's cautionary structures, built to keep expanding its own mandate.
Remember what we were warned about the military industrial complex?
## The "Ally" That Spies Like An Enemy
In June, the Pentagon's own intelligence arm rated Israeli espionage against the United States "critical" -- its **highest threat tier** , the same one reserved for the worst adversaries -- after spyware turned up on the phones of US officials shaping Iran policy. One senior official called the scale and audacity of the espionage effort "**unhinged**."
Section 219 creates a Pentagon office whose _entire job is to accelerate technology-sharing with the same country_ -- and whose authority, according to policy analysts examining the bill, would outrank the Defense Technology Security Administration, the office that's supposed to say no.
Smith isn't wrong that a handful of existing missile-defense and counter-drone programs are co-developed with Israel today, or that a single coordinating official doesn't, by itself, create a new procurement line. Chairman Mike Rogers has made the identical point. But that argument answers a question nobody serious is asking. Nobody credible claims this fuses the two militaries' chains of command -- it doesn't, and saying so hands the provision's defenders an easy rebuttal.
The real question is narrower and harder to wave away: **what happens when the technologies doing the integrating are the ones that see the battlefield, decide what counts as a threat, and usurp the data that trains the algorithm?** A standardized bullet gauge is a standardized bullet gauge. Interchangeable rifles is one thing. But a shared targeting system is a _standing dependency_ -- on someone else's data, someone else's code, someone else's judgment about who gets flagged, and necessarily involving someone else's eyes on your most sensitive military information -- someone whose national interests may not be aligned with ours.
The House passed H.R. 8800 -- the FY2027 NDAA carrying Section 219 -- on July 22, 2026 by a vote of 216 to 212. The day before, **the House Rules Committee declined to let a bipartisan amendment from Reps. Thomas Massie and Ro Khanna come to the floor at all** -- the one amendment that would have stripped Section 219 out entirely. _Members never got to vote on it._ They only got to vote on the whole bill, integration and all.
## Six Programs, or the Entire Brain?
Here is the sleight of hand Smith deployed, stated clearly:
The Pentagon's total program count is a meaningless denominator. A missile-defense radar and a rifle sling both count as "programs." But your toenail is different than your brain.
Measuring foreign entanglement by dividing by every program the Department of Defense touches is like reassuring a hospital's patients that only a handful of its thousand systems involve anesthesia, patient records, blood supply, neurosurgery, and the emergency room -- _so what 's everyone so worked up about?_
The legislation is written to produce more, not fewer, of these programs. "Expand and accelerate" is the operative language, not "maintain." Smith's own starting count -- three, four, maybe five or six, he wasn't sure -- describes a starting point, not an ending point.
**Networked technologies don 't stay in their lane.** They control everything else. Cyber tools, shared data pipelines, and AI systems feed into other weapons, other commands, other decisions, in ways the same bullet gauge never did.
And once a capability becomes a program of record, it grows contractors, budgets, and training pipelines around it. That's not a bureaucratic detail -- it's what makes a "temporary" arrangement expensive and politically painful to unwind five years later, a situation known in technology as "functional permanence," regardless of who's president or what the public thinks by then.
None of this requires believing in a secret plot. It requires reading what "expand and accelerate" actually commits the Pentagon to do.
## Adam Smith's Two Positions
Here's what makes Smith's Breaking Points answer worse than just a bad argument -- it directly contradicts the position he'd already taken in public.
Smith cosponsored H.R. 8800 -- the bill carrying Section 219 -- with Chairman Rogers back in May. At committee markup, he defended the underlying cooperation. When Rep. Ro Khanna introduced a bill in committee -- in Smith's committee! -- to remove Section 219, Smith ensured that amendment died, by _unrecorded voice vote._
By mid-July, he was telling reporters and constituents he'd reversed course, after my video about Section 224 went viral. He claimed that after hearing from people in our district about what deepening military ties to the Netanyahu government would signal right now, he'd changed his mind and would push to strip the provision in conference.
An incumbent with 35 years in elected office had to have known that by the time he publicly committed to vote against the provision on the House Floor, the damage had already been done. No serious contention would be allowed to arise in the full House.
Even so - six days later, on the eve of final passage, he sat down with a national audience and described the very same provision as barely worth discussing -- a footnote of three to six programs lost in a sea of thousands, and called concern about it "an exaggeration." He did not describe a dangerous overreach he'd fight to kill. He described something trivial.
You don't get to have it both ways. Either the provision matters enough that you reversed your public position and pledged to fight it in conference -- or it's genuinely just a handful of boots-and-uniforms programs not worth the country's attention. Smith told two different audiences two different stories in the same week, and the version he gave the cameras the day before the vote was the reassuring one, not the alarmed one.
He also had more leverage than he used. As ranking member, Smith is one of the handful of people in either chamber with a real seat at the table when the House and Senate reconcile their competing defense bills. He _says_ he'll advocate for removing Section 219 there. He has not committed to opposing a final bill that keeps it.
And he never had to force the issue in July: as ranking member on a committee producing an $1.15 trillion bill, "I'm in the minority" explains why he didn't control the floor schedule -- it doesn't explain why he chose, in the one unscripted setting the public actually saw, to minimize rather than sound the alarm.
When the bill passed the next day, Smith voted no -- but by his own public account, that vote was about the administration's Iran war and the bill's ballooning topline, not Section 219. **The one provision he 'd told constituents he'd reversed on didn't cost him a single public vote.** It rode through the House intact, and the record shows Smith telling the country, on the record, not to worry about it.
## It's Not Just the Pentagon Bill
Section 219 doesn't stand alone. A companion track is moving through the Senate Intelligence Committee: Section 622 of the FY2027 Intelligence Authorization Act, advanced by Chairman Tom Cotton, which would direct the President -- through the Director of National Intelligence -- to "expand and enhance" intelligence sharing with Israel across cyber threats, terrorism, missile and drone activity, and regional early-warning systems.
It goes further than sharing more: **it would make it harder for any future president to pull back**. Suspending or reducing that sharing would require a specific, documented national-security justification and formal notice to Congress within fifteen days.
Put the two tracks together and the picture sharpens. Intelligence is the fuel. AI and data fusion are the processing layer. Precision weapons and autonomous systems are where it's delivered.
Analyzing the defense-technology bill without the intelligence bill next to it means looking at only one piece of a system built to work as a whole.
## The Timeline Nobody's Showing You Together
Three things are converging this year, on three different legal tracks, and no one is being asked to consider them side by side.
**November 3, 2026 -- the midterm election.
** Highly likely to be a site of authoritarian interference.
**Mid-to-late December 2026 -- automatic Selective Service registration takes effect.**
This isn't part of the NDAA fight; it was already signed into law in the previous year's defense bill, in December 2025, sponsored by Rep. Chrissy Houlahan. Starting around December 18, the government will register nearly every male citizen and resident between 18 and 25 automatically, using federal data matches, instead of waiting for them to register themselves. Now, this does not reinstate a draft; Congress would still have to act separately to authorize one. What it does is remove the gaps and delays in the existing registry, so that if a future Congress ever did authorize a draft, the government would already have a far more complete list ready to go at a moment's notice. Likely, given DOGE's scope, integrated on the back-end with databases of everything else the Federal Government knows about you.
**On a separate track, still unresolved** -- **Congress has to reconcile the House and Senate defense bills before Section 219 would go into effect**.
There's no fixed date for that, before or after December 18. The Senate hasn't even started floor debate on its own NDAA: a procedural vote to begin consideration failed 50-46 in mid-July, ten votes short of the sixty needed -- the first time in 66 years the defense bill has failed a Senate cloture vote at all -- with senators including Bernie Sanders, Chris Van Hollen, Elizabeth Warren, and Ed Markey withholding support in part because they wanted Section 1217 stripped or debated on its own terms first.
As of this writing, no House-Senate conference has even begun. Congress usually finishes the NDAA in a lame-duck session after the election, which would put final negotiations sometime in November or December -- but this year's bill is already running behind that pattern, and if the impasse continues, final passage could slip past the December registration date, past the end of the year, or into the new Congress in January.
None of these three tracks proves the other two. I'm not telling you Congress has scheduled a draft, or that a secret plan links an election to a registry to a weapons-integration office. Nobody has shown that, and I won't pretend otherwise.
What I am telling you is that in the same twelve-month window, Congress is completing the machinery for faster mobilization at home while advancing a permanent, expanding technology and intelligence subordination abroad -- and asking for remarkably little public debate on either one.
That convergence is real, whatever caused it, and it deserves to be seen whole instead of as three unrelated news stories.
## Who Actually Holds the Pen Right Now
This still isn't finished, and it isn't being decided by nine people whose names never appear in a headline. It's being decided by --
In the Senate:
**Roger Wicker** , chairman of Armed Services, and **Jack Reed,** its ranking Democrat, control what the Senate's version looks like. Majority Leader **John Thune** and Minority Leader **Chuck Schumer** control when and how it comes back to the floor, and what amendments get an actual vote. **Sanders** , **Van Hollen** , **Warren** , **Markey** , **Jeff Merkley** , and **Peter Welch** are the senators currently withholding support specifically over these provisions.
In the House-Senate conference still to come:
**Rogers** , **Smith** , **Wicker** , and **Reed** will be the four people at the table deciding whether Section 219/1217 survives, gets narrowed, or gets cut. **A provision can appear in both chambers ' bills and still disappear in conference** -- but only if the people who negotiate it choose to let it go.
**At the finish line** : the President can sign or veto the whole bill, but cannot line-item-veto just this section -- not that he would. By the time it reaches his desk, it's this or nothing.
_**If you want this provision gone, those are the names to call.**_
## The Ripples Go Far Beyond Us
This argument has implications for American integrity as well as American sovereignty. The technologies this initiative would deepen -- AI-assisted targeting, mass surveillance, autonomous drone and missile systems -- have been used for years to perpetrate well-documented war crimes amounting to a genocide against a civilian population living under occupation and bombardment.
**Congress is proposing to lock in deeper subservience on exactly those systems with exactly that perpetrating entity, before it has required any real accounting for how American taxpayer dollars have already been used.**
"Lethal technology" isn't morally neutral just because it's useful. If American intelligence, code, or hardware plays a role in a strike, the American public has a right to know whose rules governed that decision and who's accountable when it's wrong.
## The MINIMUM Congress Should Do
* Strike the executive-agent provision, or at minimum require it to come back for a standalone, recorded vote -- not a rider nobody gets to vote on separately.
* Reject any language that limits a future president's ability to reduce intelligence sharing based on the facts on the ground.
* Require a public accounting of every program covered by the initiative, updated annually, not just an internal report to two committees.
* Require independent, public audits of any AI targeting system's training data and civilian-harm safeguards before it's adopted.
* Bar U.S. data, technology, or intelligence from supporting operations that violate U.S. or international law -- full stop, not "except in this appropriations bill."
* Require congressional **authorization** , not just notification, before jointly developed systems become permanent U.S. programs of record.
* Put a sunset date on the whole initiative, so no Congress locks out a future Congress from changing its mind.

And I'd ask Adam Smith directly: if you believed in July that this provision mattered enough to reverse your position, why did you spend your one national platform the week of the vote telling people it didn't? Which was the real answer -- the one you gave your constituents, or the one you gave the cameras?
Or the one you gave when you explained the reversal by pointing to ["the tactics used by those on the far left"](https://substack.com/redirect/718e300c-e161-4f95-945f-c47bbfb61d97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- the same left he's [called "fascists" who should be arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/b4806867-264d-49ab-9503-8311b0f19c2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a comment the [43rd District Democrats officially condemned him for](https://substack.com/redirect/1b022eeb-3a1a-43b1-a43c-71909be24c8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) back [in 2024](https://substack.com/redirect/80bfae03-e488-4469-adb8-b46095646fc4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Was the flip-flopping really about the provision -- or about managing a primary against a wholehearted peace activist, wife and daughter of American heros and disabled American veterans, who has the moral courage to call this out and the integrity not to take money from the interests that want to further violate American sovereignty and international law?
**Congress does not get to build the architecture for the next war by burying it in a thousand-page bill nobody gets a clean vote on, in the same season it automates the registry for who dies in it.**
**Democracy isn 't consent after the fact. It's a public, accountable debate before the switch gets flipped -- not a press release after.**
**Care. Courage. The Constitution.**

The "Ally" That Spies Like An Enemy In June, the Pentagon's own intelligence arm rated Israeli espionage against the United States "critical" -- its highest threat tier , the same one reserved for the worst adversaries -- after spyware turned up on the phones of US officials shaping Iran policy. One senior official called the scale and audacity of the espionage effort "unhinged." Section 219 creates a Pentagon office whose entire job is to accelerate technology-sharing with the same country -- and whose authority, according to policy analysts examining the bill, would outrank the Defense Technology Security Administration, the office that's supposed to say no. Smith isn't wrong that a handful of existing missile-defense and counter-drone programs are co-developed with Israel today, or that a single coordinating official doesn't, by itself, create a new procurement line. Chairman Mike Rogers has made the identical point. But that argument answers a question nobody serious is asking. Nobody credible claims this fuses the two militaries' chains of command -- it doesn't, and saying so hands the provision's defenders an easy rebuttal. The real question is narrower and harder to wave away: what happens when the technologies doing the integrating are the ones that see the battlefield, decide what counts as a threat, and usurp the data that trains the algorithm? A standardized bullet gauge is a standardized bullet gauge. Interchangeable rifles is one thing. But a shared targeting system is a standing dependency -- on someone else's data, someone else's code, someone else's judgment about who gets flagged, and necessarily involving someone else's eyes on your most sensitive military information -- someone whose national interests may not be aligned with ours. The House passed H.R. 8800 -- the FY2027 NDAA carrying Section 219 -- on July 22, 2026 by a vote of 216 to 212. The day before, the House Rules Committee declined to let a bipartisan amendment from Reps. Thomas Massie and Ro Khanna come to the floor at all -- the one amendment that would have stripped Section 219 out entirely. Members never got to vote on it. They only got to vote on the whole bill, integration and all. Six Programs, or the Entire Brain? Here is the sleight of hand Smith deployed, stated clearly: The Pentagon's total program count is a meaningless denominator. A missile-defense radar and a rifle sling both count as "programs." But your toenail is different than your brain. Measuring foreign entanglement by dividing by every program the Department of Defense touches is like reassuring a hospital's patients that only a handful of its thousand systems involve anesthesia, patient records, blood supply, neurosurgery, and the emergency room -- so what 's everyone so worked up about? The legislation is written to produce more, not fewer, of these programs. "Expand and accelerate" is the operative language, not "maintain." Smith's own starting count -- three, four, maybe five or six, he wasn't sure -- describes a starting point, not an ending point. Networked technologies don 't stay in their lane. They control everything else. Cyber tools, shared data pipelines, and AI systems feed into other weapons, other commands, other decisions, in ways the same bullet gauge never did. And once a capability becomes a program of record, it grows contractors, budgets, and training pipelines around it. That's not a bureaucratic detail -- it's what makes a "temporary" arrangement expensive and politically painful to unwind five years later, a situation known in technology as "functional permanence," regardless of who's president or what the public thinks by then. None of this requires believing in a secret plot. It requires reading what "expand and accelerate" actually commits the Pentagon to do. Adam Smith's Two Positions Here's what makes Smith's Breaking Points answer worse than just a bad argument -- it directly contradicts the position he'd already taken in public. Smith cosponsored H.R. 8800 -- the bill carrying Section 219 -- with Chairman Rogers back in May. At committee markup, he defended the underlying cooperation. When Rep. Ro Khanna introduced a bill in committee -- in Smith's committee! -- to remove Section 219, Smith ensured that amendment died, by unrecorded voice vote. By mid-July, he was telling reporters and constituents he'd reversed course, after my video about Section 224 went viral. He claimed that after hearing from people in our district about what deepening military ties to the Netanyahu government would signal right now, he'd changed his mind and would push to strip the provision in conference. An incumbent with 35 years in elected office had to have known that by the time he publicly committed to vote against the provision on the House Floor, the damage had already been done. No serious contention would be allowed to arise in the full House. Even so - six days later, on the eve of final passage, he sat down with a national audience and described the very same provision as barely worth discussing -- a footnote of three to six programs lost in a sea of thousands, and called concern about it "an exaggeration." He did not describe a dangerous overreach he'd fight to kill. He described something trivial. You don't get to have it both ways. Either the provision matters enough that you reversed your public position and pledged to fight it in conference -- or it's genuinely just a handful of boots-and-uniforms programs not worth the country's attention. Smith told two different audiences two different stories in the same week, and the version he gave the cameras the day before the vote was the reassuring one, not the alarmed one. He also had more leverage than he used. As ranking member, Smith is one of the handful of people in either chamber with a real seat at the table when the House and Senate reconcile their competing defense bills. He says he'll advocate for removing Section 219 there. He has not committed to opposing a final bill that keeps it. And he never had to force the issue in July: as ranking member on a committee producing an $1.15 trillion bill, "I'm in the minority" explains why he didn't control the floor schedule -- it doesn't explain why he chose, in the one unscripted setting the public actually saw, to minimize rather than sound the alarm. When the bill passed the next day, Smith voted no -- but by his own public account, that vote was about the administration's Iran war and the bill's ballooning topline, not Section 219. The one provision he 'd told constituents he'd reversed on didn't cost him a single public vote. It rode through the House intact, and the record shows Smith telling the country, on the record, not to worry about it. It's Not Just the Pentagon Bill Section 219 doesn't stand alone. A companion track is moving through the Senate Intelligence Committee: Section 622 of the FY2027 Intelligence Authorization Act, advanced by Chairman Tom Cotton, which would direct the President -- through the Director of National Intelligence -- to "expand and enhance" intelligence sharing with Israel across cyber threats, terrorism, missile and drone activity, and regional early-warning systems. It goes further than sharing more: it would make it harder for any future president to pull back. Suspending or reducing that sharing would require a specific, documented national-security justification and formal notice to Congress within fifteen days. Put the two tracks together and the picture sharpens. Intelligence is the fuel. AI and data fusion are the processing layer. Precision weapons and autonomous systems are where it's delivered. Analyzing the defense-technology bill without the intelligence bill next to it means looking at only one piece of a system built to work as a whole. The Timeline Nobody's Showing You Together Three things are converging this year, on three different legal tracks, and no one is being asked to consider them side by side. November 3, 2026 -- the midterm election. Highly likely to be a site of authoritarian interference. Mid-to-late December 2026 -- automatic Selective Service registration takes effect. This isn't part of the NDAA fight; it was already signed into law in the previous year's defense bill, in December 2025, sponsored by Rep. Chrissy Houlahan. Starting around December 18, the government will register nearly every male citizen and resident between 18 and 25 automatically, using federal data matches, instead of waiting for them to register themselves. Now, this does not reinstate a draft; Congress would still have to act separately to authorize one. What it does is remove the gaps and delays in the existing registry, so that if a future Congress ever did authorize a draft, the government would already have a far more complete list ready to go at a moment's notice. Likely, given DOGE's scope, integrated on the back-end with databases of everything else the Federal Government knows about you. On a separate track, still unresolved -- Congress has to reconcile the House and Senate defense bills before Section 219 would go into effect. There's no fixed date for that, before or after December 18. The Senate hasn't even started floor debate on its own NDAA: a procedural vote to begin consideration failed 50-46 in mid-July, ten votes short of the sixty needed -- the first time in 66 years the defense bill has failed a Senate cloture vote at all -- with senators including Bernie Sanders, Chris Van Hollen, Elizabeth Warren, and Ed Markey withholding support in part because they wanted Section 1217 stripped or debated on its own terms first. As of this writing, no House-Senate conference has even begun. Congress usually finishes the NDAA in a lame-duck session after the election, which would put final negotiations sometime in November or December -- but this year's bill is already running behind that pattern, and if the impasse continues, final passage could slip past the December registration date, past the end of the year, or into the new Congress in January. None of these three tracks proves the other two. I'm not telling you Congress has scheduled a draft, or that a secret plan links an election to a registry to a weapons-integration office. Nobody has shown that, and I won't pretend otherwise. What I am telling you is that in the same twelve-month window, Congress is completing the machinery for faster mobilization at home while advancing a permanent, expanding technology and intelligence subordination abroad -- and asking for remarkably little public debate on either one. That convergence is real, whatever caused it, and it deserves to be seen whole instead of as three unrelated news stories. Who Actually Holds the Pen Right Now This still isn't finished, and it isn't being decided by nine people whose names never appear in a headline. It's being decided by -- In the Senate: Roger Wicker , chairman of Armed Services, and Jack Reed, its ranking Democrat, control what the Senate's version looks like. Majority Leader John Thune and Minority Leader Chuck Schumer control when and how it comes back to the floor, and what amendments get an actual vote. Sanders , Van Hollen , Warren , Markey , Jeff Merkley , and Peter Welch are the senators currently withholding support specifically over these provisions. In the House-Senate conference still to come: Rogers , Smith , Wicker , and Reed will be the four people at the table deciding whether Section 219/1217 survives, gets narrowed, or gets cut. A provision can appear in both chambers ' bills and still disappear in conference -- but only if the people who negotiate it choose to let it go. At the finish line : the President can sign or veto the whole bill, but cannot line-item-veto just this section -- not that he would. By the time it reaches his desk, it's this or nothing. If you want this provision gone, those are the names to call. The Ripples Go Far Beyond Us This argument has implications for American integrity as well as American sovereignty. The technologies this initiative would deepen -- AI-assisted targeting, mass surveillance, autonomous drone and missile systems -- have been used for years to perpetrate well-documented war crimes amounting to a genocide against a civilian population living under occupation and bombardment. Congress is proposing to lock in deeper subservience on exactly those systems with exactly that perpetrating entity, before it has required any real accounting for how American taxpayer dollars have already been used. "Lethal technology" isn't morally neutral just because it's useful. If American intelligence, code, or hardware plays a role in a strike, the American public has a right to know whose rules governed that decision and who's accountable when it's wrong. The MINIMUM Congress Should Do Strike the executive-agent provision, or at minimum require it to come back for a standalone, recorded vote -- not a rider nobody gets to vote on separately. Reject any language that limits a future president's ability to reduce intelligence sharing based on the facts on the ground. Require a public accounting of every program covered by the initiative, updated annually, not just an internal report to two committees. Require independent, public audits of any AI targeting system's training data and civilian-harm safeguards before it's adopted. Bar U.S. data, technology, or intelligence from supporting operations that violate U.S. or international law -- full stop, not "except in this appropriations bill." Require congressional authorization , not just notification, before jointly developed systems become permanent U.S. programs of record. Put a sunset date on the whole initiative, so no Congress locks out a future Congress from changing its mind. And I'd ask Adam Smith directly: if you believed in July that this provision mattered enough to reverse your position, why did you spend your one national platform the week of the vote telling people it didn't? Which was the real answer -- the one you gave your constituents, or the one you gave the cameras? Or the one you gave when you explained the reversal by pointing to -- the same left he's , a comment the back . Was the flip-flopping really about the provision -- or about managing a primary against a wholehearted peace activist, wife and daughter of American heros and disabled American veterans, who has the moral courage to call this out and the integrity not to take money from the interests that want to further violate American sovereignty and international law? Congress does not get to build the architecture for the next war by burying it in a thousand-page bill nobody gets a clean vote on, in the same season it automates the registry for who dies in it. Democracy isn 't consent after the fact. It's a public, accountable debate before the switch gets flipped -- not a press release after. Care. Courage. ### Evidence Grows Exposing Coordinated Scheme of Voter Intimidation and Ballot Influence
The latest disclosure from the Stearns County Sheriff's Office make one point crystal clear: the chaotic activities surrounding elections in the St. Cloud area are not confined to a single polling place or a single county. When considered together with the Sherburne County [Sheriff's investigation](https://open.substack.com/pub/bendasense/p/voting-chaos-in-minnesota?r=1rusnm&utm_campaign=post-expanded-share&utm_medium=web), this new evidence reveals a recurring pattern of voter influence and polling-place disruption extending throughout the greater St. Cloud region.
As the map below demonstrates, the City of St. Cloud spans Stearns, Sherburne, and Benton Counties, placing three separate election jurisdictions within a single metropolitan area. This unique arrangement creates an environment in which organized groups can move voters across county lines, operate between multiple polling locations, and pressure-test election administration processes in more than one jurisdiction. The proximity of three separate voting entities in a large population center creates an ideal environment for a _**bus, influence, and ballot harvest**_ operation to florish.

### Stearns County Reports Reveal New Evidence of Illegal Voter Influence Operation
We've all seen the headlines highlighting the laudable goals of voter outreach, accessibility, and assistance for those who legitimately need help casting a ballot. But describing the network now coming to light as a voter-protection effort does not square with the evidence. Additional sheriff's investigations paint a far different picture.
There are two new reports that merit review.
The first arises from an election complaint submitted in Stearns County and referred to the Stearns County Sheriff's Office for investigation. The resulting witness interviews provide _**new firsthand accounts**_ that expand upon the events previously reported.
1. A Stearns County election official reported that "herself, her associate, and a representative from the City of St. Cloud has spoken to [The Teacher]... about hanging out inside and outside of the polling location several times during the early voting period."
2. Stearns County election officials received a call from the DFL Director of Voter Protection who forwarded a complaint that, "interpreters are telling voters who to vote for."
3. One voter interviewed stated that, "she overheard individuals telling voters who to vote for." As is a common-theme, this woman was very "nervous" and concerned that her conversation would become "public."
4. Another voter reported: 1) as she entered the polling place she was approached by people who were asking her who she was voting for and trying to influence her vote; 2) that she saw and heard these same people approach voters (inside and outside the polling place) telling them who to vote for; and 3) the nervous voter asked if her interview would be "public."
5. A concerned citizen went to the Lake George Polling place and personally observed _The Teacher_ "right inside the entrance to the building and next to the room where the voting was taking place... telling people to vote for [his wife]."
6. Another revealing statement from a Stearns County election official was detailed in the report, "election judges have a difficult time understanding what is being said to the other individuals of the Somali community members as they are speaking in their native language."

The second report describes an alleged double-voting incident in Stearns County. A husband and wife were escorted to separate polling locations on two different occasions. They first completed absentee ballots on September 23, 2024. On Election Day, November 5, 2024, they again cast ballots after completing Election Day registrations using a new address. The facts as detailed below, are very similar to the [Sherburne County double vote](https://open.substack.com/pub/bendasense/p/breaking-384-page-report-details?r=1rusnm&utm_campaign=post-expanded-share&utm_medium=web):
* They were transported to the polling place by someone they did not know.
* Once they arrived at the polling place they were handed off to a different man, who escorted them into the polling place and controlled the voting process.
* Their poll escort completed their absentee application for them and used an address that was not where they lived.
* "Once she got the ballot, the Somali male completed the ballot for her, and nothing was ever explained to her about what was happening."
* On election day, wife was approached by the "same person" who drove her to a different polling place and handed her off to another escort, which she reported, "The male who was helping her took her ballot and they walked to a booth where they voted. She described the male who helped her made all the selections on the ballot and never explained what happened."

### This Was Not a Simple Get-Out-the-Vote Operation
Taken together, the Stearns County and Sherburne County reports document a recurring pattern that crosses county lines. They describe organized transportation of groups of voters, the repeated appearance of the same self-described "interpreters" at multiple polling locations, and repeated concerns from election officials about improper influence inside polling places. The conduct described in these investigations goes well beyond the customary role of voter outreach or assistance.
Rather than isolated acts by overzealous volunteers, the reports describe recurring conduct involving the same methods, the same group of participants, and similar concerns across multiple jurisdictions. The pattern suggests organization, coordination, and repetition--not coincidence.
In my previous reporting, I focused on the Sherburne County portion of this operation, including the "caught-on-camera" double vote, escorted by individuals identified as "the Teacher" and "the Man in Black." The newly released Stearns County Sheriff's confirms that the Sherburne County double vote was not a one-time incident.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0c147c69-940b-4653-ba2d-3024f5f9b25a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This was not a neighborhood get-out-the-vote effort. This was closer to a _Peaky Blinders_ operation--where a coordinated network of individuals brazenly force members of their community to follow orders. Drivers recruit and transport voters, escorted them into polling place. They then either escort them or hand them off to other operatives, who remain with voters throughout the voting process. These handlers fill out the ballots for the voters and appear to confirm that they have voted as instructed. Viewed individually, each act may appear ordinary. Viewed together, the reports reveal a coordinated syndicate-style operation.
### Multi-County Scheme Lures Vulnerable voters into Breaking Voting Laws
Perhaps most troubling is what happens to the vulnerable voters themselves. These individuals are allegedly manipulated, intimidated, and persuaded into violating election laws they often do not fully understand. In the end, they are forced to make an impossible choice: defy the neighborhood lieutenants orchestrating the operation, or risk becoming the person held accountable if law enforcement uncovers the scheme.
The evidence suggests that many caught in this scheme fear the consequences imposed by community enforcers far more than those imposed by government authorities. That is precisely why the secrecy of the ballot exists--to protect every voter from coercion, intimidation, and undue influence.
Yet instead of confronting these allegations and restoring confidence in the electoral process, election officials have largely responded with denial. Despite multiple documented incidents investigated across more than one county, one Sherburne [County official dismissed](https://substack.com/redirect/504bdb6d-9aa7-4fb6-84e9-96fd7c40b2e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the matter as "_one past, isolated incident that did not rise to the level of disorder or disruption of voting privileges and rights, let alone any violation of state law._ "
The growing body of reports from both Sherburne and Stearns Counties tells a different story--one that demands serious scrutiny rather than bureacratic double-speak. Even local St. Cloud area media outlets are starting to discuss the uncomfortable truth that St. Cloud has a problem. A [recent headline ](https://substack.com/redirect/2888b8d7-b8fd-4aee-b0fb-d52ee2730bfc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)describes it as: "**Voter-Pressure Complaints. " **As described in that article,
"The Stearns County records add to the picture that emerged from Sherburne County, in which voter assistance, including rides, interpreters, and help with paperwork, repeatedly drew the attention of election officials and investigators across county lines."
It appears that [previous calls](https://substack.com/redirect/d0b97bd3-dfeb-47c6-b130-db3af7956a01?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for local election officials to station sergeants-at-arms at polling places have reached a bureaucratic dead end. If local officials are unwilling to act, it is time for state or federal authorities to step in.
No voter should have to choose between obeying the law and obeying a person who escorts them into the polling place. No election judge should have to wonder whether the rules inside the polling place will be respected. And no community should be expected to accept repeated reports of intimidation and improper influence without demanding accountability and reform. The ballot belongs to the voter--not to the person standing beside them.

When considered together with the Sherburne County , this new evidence reveals a recurring pattern of voter influence and polling-place disruption extending throughout the greater St. Cloud region. This unique arrangement creates an environment in which organized groups can move voters across county lines, operate between multiple polling locations, and pressure-test election administration processes in more than one jurisdiction. But describing the network now coming to light as a voter-protection effort does not square with the evidence. Additional sheriff's investigations paint a far different picture. There are two new reports that merit review. The first arises from an election complaint submitted in Stearns County and referred to the Stearns County Sheriff's Office for investigation. The resulting witness interviews provide new firsthand accounts that expand upon the events previously reported. 1. A Stearns County election official reported that "herself, her associate, and a representative from the City of St. Cloud has spoken to [The Teacher]... about hanging out inside and outside of the polling location several times during the early voting period." 2. Stearns County election officials received a call from the DFL Director of Voter Protection who forwarded a complaint that, "interpreters are telling voters who to vote for." 3. One voter interviewed stated that, "she overheard individuals telling voters who to vote for." As is a common-theme, this woman was very "nervous" and concerned that her conversation would become "public." 4. Another voter reported: 1) as she entered the polling place she was approached by people who were asking her who she was voting for and trying to influence her vote; 2) that she saw and heard these same people approach voters (inside and outside the polling place) telling them who to vote for; and 3) the nervous voter asked if her interview would be "public." 5. A concerned citizen went to the Lake George Polling place and personally observed The Teacher "right inside the entrance to the building and next to the room where the voting was taking place... telling people to vote for [his wife]." 6. Another revealing statement from a Stearns County election official was detailed in the report, "election judges have a difficult time understanding what is being said to the other individuals of the Somali community members as they are speaking in their native language." | Stearns County Report Election Complaint...404KB ∙ PDF file ---|--- | The second report describes an alleged double-voting incident in Stearns County. A husband and wife were escorted to separate polling locations on two different occasions. They first completed absentee ballots on September 23, 2024. On Election Day, November 5, 2024, they again cast ballots after completing Election Day registrations using a new address. The facts as detailed below, are very similar to the : They were transported to the polling place by someone they did not know. Once they arrived at the polling place they were handed off to a different man, who escorted them into the polling place and controlled the voting process. Their poll escort completed their absentee application for them and used an address that was not where they lived. "Once she got the ballot, the Somali male completed the ballot for her, and nothing was ever explained to her about what was happening." On election day, wife was approached by the "same person" who drove her to a different polling place and handed her off to another escort, which she reported, "The male who was helping her took her ballot and they walked to a booth where they voted. She described the male who helped her made all the selections on the ballot and never explained what happened." | Stearns County Case Report H&w Double Vo...3.04MB ∙ PDF file ---|--- | This Was Not a Simple Get-Out-the-Vote Operation Taken together, the Stearns County and Sherburne County reports document a recurring pattern that crosses county lines. They describe organized transportation of groups of voters, the repeated appearance of the same self-described "interpreters" at multiple polling locations, and repeated concerns from election officials about improper influence inside polling places. The conduct described in these investigations goes well beyond the customary role of voter outreach or assistance. Rather than isolated acts by overzealous volunteers, the reports describe recurring conduct involving the same methods, the same group of participants, and similar concerns across multiple jurisdictions. The pattern suggests organization, coordination, and repetition--not coincidence. In my previous reporting, I focused on the Sherburne County portion of this operation, including the "caught-on-camera" double vote, escorted by individuals identified as "the Teacher" and "the Man in Black." The newly released Stearns County Sheriff's confirms that the Sherburne County double vote was not a one-time incident. | | ---|---|--- This was not a neighborhood get-out-the-vote effort. This was closer to a Peaky Blinders operation--where a coordinated network of individuals brazenly force members of their community to follow orders. Drivers recruit and transport voters, escorted them into polling place. They then either escort them or hand them off to other operatives, who remain with voters throughout the voting process. These handlers fill out the ballots for the voters and appear to confirm that they have voted as instructed. Viewed individually, each act may appear ordinary. Viewed together, the reports reveal a coordinated syndicate-style operation. Multi-County Scheme Lures Vulnerable voters into Breaking Voting Laws Perhaps most troubling is what happens to the vulnerable voters themselves. These individuals are allegedly manipulated, intimidated, and persuaded into violating election laws they often do not fully understand. In the end, they are forced to make an impossible choice: defy the neighborhood lieutenants orchestrating the operation, or risk becoming the person held accountable if law enforcement uncovers the scheme. The evidence suggests that many caught in this scheme fear the consequences imposed by community enforcers far more than those imposed by government authorities. That is precisely why the secrecy of the ballot exists--to protect every voter from coercion, intimidation, and undue influence. Yet instead of confronting these allegations and restoring confidence in the electoral process, election officials have largely responded with denial. Despite multiple documented incidents investigated across more than one county, one Sherburne the matter as "one past, isolated incident that did not rise to the level of disorder or disruption of voting privileges and rights, let alone any violation of state law. " The growing body of reports from both Sherburne and Stearns Counties tells a different story--one that demands serious scrutiny rather than bureacratic double-speak. Even local St. Cloud area media outlets are starting to discuss the uncomfortable truth that St. Cloud has a problem. A it as: "Voter-Pressure Complaints. " **As described in that article, "The Stearns County records add to the picture that emerged from Sherburne County, in which voter assistance, including rides, interpreters, and help with paperwork, repeatedly drew the attention of election officials and investigators across county lines." It appears that for local election officials to station sergeants-at-arms at polling places have reached a bureaucratic dead end. If local officials are unwilling to act, it is time for state or federal authorities to step in. No voter should have to choose between obeying the law and obeying a person who escorts them into the polling place. No election judge should have to wonder whether the rules inside the polling place will be respected. And no community should be expected to accept repeated reports of intimidation and improper influence without demanding accountability and reform. The ballot belongs to the voter--not to the person standing beside them. Matt Benda. @Bendasense Substack is a reader-supported publication. name: Michael Baumgartner
subject: Prayers for those impacted by the devastating fires.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Vote Baumgartner for Congress | www
body:
Thank you to the first responders and all those stepping up to help.

| | | | | | | The fires in Spokane and across Eastern Washington have been an unprecedented and devastating tragedy, uprooting thousands of people and destroying hundreds of homes.Today I worked cooperatively with U.S. Senator Maria Cantwell, Spokane Mayor Lisa Brown, Gov. Bob Ferguson, Spokane County Sheriff John Nowels, and our first responders for a coordinated bipartisan response.
I spoke with Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and White House officials today to ensure federal authorities are closely tracking the situation.
I am pleased that Governor Ferguson had a productive and positive conversation with President Trump and I will be strongly and actively supporting our request for federal assistance to those impacted by these fires.
Both Eleanor and I also hold in our hearts and prayers the families disrupted and those whose homes were damaged, and we are grateful for the first responders who have worked all hours to protect our community.
We know that while this is unprecedented devastation for the Spokane area, our community also always rallies to support each other in times of need. We urge you to do what you can to support those in need by donating through organizations like the Red Cross and 2nd Harvest Food Bank.
It is also worth noting that while the fires in Spokane county have been terrible, many others are suffering across Eastern Washington including in Stevens County, the Colville Reservation, the Spokane Tribe Reservation and other areas.
Please do what you can to help our friends and neighbors during this difficult time.
God Bless,
Michael

Peter,
On Monday, the Trump administration marched into the Supreme Court and begged to the justices to let him gut mail-in voting before the November election.
It's the same demented obsession that has consumed this man since 2020 just repackaged for the dozenth time: an executive order that would let the federal government decide who gets a mail ballot, by forcing the Postal Service to mail ballots only to voters whose names appear on "citizenship lists" compiled by his very own administration.

| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Pr-i79u81hVWLdJQRxbTX3HoKMGconBqNZy8C_aUX7FAAHM25lmc3QyDL5_adyJaCGg2yFsMRNBGXWZmolamSOFYqgQfkGfBbrpJeMj9oHq171emIRYJ4BWOVnslFT-X6lU8luxBDuNf8z5EbDQYxErrHPt0xZNkYGd22u1y4d5xw-wXogFzi1X5OY88r28Mq0kGA5lT7I8Eg0FB5Q6fqs7urRazQJLmZbaCk-5Y410=&c=j6rKdz275ZNNskuCAXzfIxfGTMg4eka6xFg3-792zCe6WGq9iEJN4A==&ch=7Amxd960vRppmRSjlTE9lOQjwOqYIKrhzjI1ph6mnRTibP3oEol6Sg==)

This is the move of a pathetic loser, a man so terrified of being held accountable for the disaster he's made of America and the world, and so unable to accept he's headed for a blowout, that he'd rather beg nine unelected judges to rig the game than face the voters.
Every court has told him he can't do this. A federal judge blocked it; the 1st Circuit upheld that block, warning it would "threaten disenfranchisement of many eligible voters." The Constitution gives states and Congress the power to run elections, not the president.
Yet he just keeps begging.
But there is something that is actually alarming about this latest attempt. This time he filed an emergency application, inviting SCOUTS to issue a ruling using the "shadow docket", where it can hand him a win with no signed opinion, no reasoning to scrutinize, and no precedent that could ever be used against MAGA later.
We have all seen how this Court rules. They overturned Roe. They gutted the Voting Rights Act. They handed Trump criminal immunity. This court has been fully exposed as a puppet of Trump and MAGA extremists, willing to torch a half-century of precedent to tilt elections their way.
So ask yourself: do you trust this Supreme Court to stop Trump from banning voting by mail? Neither do we.
This is exactly why Defend Our Courts exists. We are fighting on two fronts. First, building a firewall of state Supreme Courts with the power to protect free and fair elections state by state. Second, building the movement to reclaim a Court that has made itself an arm of the Trump administration.

## Trump Cancels Iran Strikes, Cites Deal
President Trump said he [canceled planned military strikes](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLuO5CAURL8GZ1g8jB8BwSbOetMNrdtw3WYbgwW32-q_H3mk-YJJKinpqE79uy03CDGkx1_Y0dKal4RnjUiEZQkFUqUSnlgdJIcRfcRad1yUUD0XIxd68RDiZ-kab1dEhbpBK4fRDEYaI5vNqh5QGSPvcpJGOq37vpN37QcYlfOTbIK9aGIUWgphjGgnmGQ_deM4eQ1GrKwT6APl0v7PIdGGa_zkN5bW5b2JdiM6KtN_mJqZms_zbF26u6tkar7QTM1ivEIxNVN57Qc_IqSEngMRuCfPiV-u_MeSw0pYeEFwW0gPnl8UQ0KeV-4RYrvRHpti_XGGGEPtB9aJxw4hfk-iX_34tuorAAD__2-Dhj4) on Iran over the weekend after negotiators reached the outline of a deal to end the conflict. The agreement would require the [complete reopening](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uwyAUBeCnsTcswGDDwNAlW7p2tG7NJabhxwISK336ylXfoOOVro7Odz6uyxV88On2DhFNc3lJeNSArWFZfIFUW_F3rCukFQPagLVGXDjlE6GK0HGx4MNrEb01DpHj2KNhs5KzZFKyfjMc3fTppNKCAZskjFQwBiNDLbXSK-u9OdOooiOjVEo6aNBs0kIpbUeQ1HWCovUtl-Er-9Q2dOGVn1iGNcc-mK21vXbjW8cvHb8cxzGchAPxfj50_NLKI-5khRAqyc6Rk0X-XMRihGTreYNvJDuy5RIf36Rg3jGhJYzzWUxa98XY_fAh-DrNnaC3CD78dmj_Gu5p-E8AAAD__2zvguQ) of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to Iran's nuclear threat, though Trump warned the U.S. military remains "locked and loaded" if talks collapse. Iran's foreign minister said Sunday that [negotiations with Oman](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFu7CAURL8Gd1gXMDYuKF7jbl-b0iLmsr4JNivA62y-PnJ-IeVopBmd83abb44i7ff_bkNbQ5p3PEvEWjHPlN1eaqZPLIvbF4zoI5ay4SxB9hwMBzV7R_E1d423AVGiatCKwehBC61Fs1qlVTAyuB5BDKKXOOAApl_efTc6WLAhe62BASUAtIZ2dKPox86Y0SunIbAO0FNNuf1ItNcVQ3ylJ-Z2SVsT7VrrozD1j8mJyek8zzakr4vi6pmcIj2RX5nJqeZje_CLi58ucyrZYeRrytvxzd1xP0rlssnWP06KkUo_sA7um6P4e1b_ZOhp5U8AAAD__4sYe5w) over the strait are in their final stages, though officials tied to the country's Revolutionary Guard denied that any deal exists. The reversal came after Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman [urged restraint](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2SozAQBeDTiAyq1UL8BAo2IfOmG1IyakzvCImSNGZ8-ynbc4MJOut69b737zJfLHsOt792J1PWOAc6s6dSKM2cbMgl8QflxYaFPDlPOe80I2BXw1CDmp1l_5jbypmVCElVZGQ_6F5LrWW1mUWvo1QKFbirWgDs0L-ud-N6xUFVbJ5pMICSAFpDM9pRdmM7DKNTVsMqWiDHJabmf-RQNlr9I94pNUvcK2-2Uo4s1B-Bk8DpPM_mtHnjcCsx0JfdObxfBU5H9Lw8BE6OVgqZBE5t16OUSuBU0ud-1G9orp_2-gdfO7Je4FQl446Tvefc9aKF227Zv1qUX013N_gdAAD___pqgrE) in a call with Trump. The shelved campaign would have targeted Iran's energy infrastructure and could have lasted several days.
## Senator Urges Ex-Son-in-Law to Resign
Sen. Bernie Moreno of Ohio [called for the resignation](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFu6zAQRE9DdTRWlCiJBYvfqPNvUwpraWVtsiQNkrHj2wf2FdINMMAM3vs4L2dk4Xj9j4F83dMS6VGEaqW8cMZYauYvKivGlYQ2oVICLQbMoGHS0C0bsjyXvtn8TmSoa8i342RH21rbNod3lw6ca5HWFgEHO9JE00gDXMi4vdsb9q81mKBrAayFk0PXDq6fJrd1aGFXPdDGNeXTZ-JYD9rlme6UT2sKjfij1ltR3T9lZmXmetDBIq9OmflIgV5A7_hdSJl5AOh7MDqkTDHpFUWK3lPWAX90YBHKOlPha8TKKSozN9lvtweLcBlG1cM1IL8PmvonY3dvfgMAAP__wbF_5A) of fellow Republican Rep. Max Miller on Sunday, declaring his former son-in-law "a danger to my daughter" and unfit for office. The rebuke came shortly after Miller [denied the allegations](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGy2yAQRb9G6tAAQhYUFGncOW1KzVqs7I0X8AAx8d-_8fuF19-5Z875c9kuQEzp9hsi-nbkLWGvjK1h2ahAqq3QA-sOaUfGwFhrxE1LfRLSCjlvAYjfmxmDPxA1ziN6tdplXdSyqPHunVP6isd-aDBg5lXKYKzWDoN0qI4wkv-8SStnJeWyyMmBUydnrHVhhkUeg5EYqOUy_c2U2h0PfucXlmnPcWR_b-1Zh_nXoM-DPvfep49CR3x8BoM-R_gvIjFjEa_cq2hZ1AYpiEihYYlVBEyEVcD1X0UBzHiDRjlVobRejXV2LD48OzFTPa2DkbcIxN_89qNoL6-_AgAA__8XrYIc) in a livestream and vowed to stay in his reelection race, saying no court or agency has substantiated any abuse claim against him. Moreno's daughter Emily, who divorced Miller last year, has [accused him in court filings](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQBuCnMdtFxjYEBg9d2NK1I7rgA9weNrKdpLx9RdU36HLLSZ_-__-4jTf07MPyjhvZMscx0CszlUJp9AlDLsl_UZ4wTMTkmHLeaFRStSA7kHp06PkYTeXsTKRIV2Tra9dcm7pp6mq1Rva6bvsazYR3R3Iyre56ZbR2rZu0rLw9NdlJXUvZNPLSY1-3vem63mls5CyMJOdLTJfP6ENZaeYjPildprhVbNdS9iz0m1CDUEM49pjL-RJqOGGhBtmdRwk1PDKc_YQaMgW4UwqeYIuJQoTZB2Q-YELmDHNMkGiHDb9h88yUoERIlP0SAOdCCVYCZKaFHB-A90cm92dliK8ADh_LWigJNVTJuv3lmX1ur8LIZUPPv_nLv0Z_WvUTAAD___ETlxA) of shoving her, pouring scalding water on her, and putting a gun to her head. Miller has sued her for defamation. The feud between the two Trump-aligned Republicans landed days before [Wednesday's deadline](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1u6zAQBODTUJ2EFSXqp2DxGnV-bUphLS3tTZakQTKWfftAuUKaaQb4BpiPy3pBFg63_-jJFhfXQEcWKoXSyglDLom_KG8YNhLahXL2tGrQQw1TDd26I8t77avdOiJNXUW2HSczmtaYtrrbzujr7siNm6bJuLmfx6sG6Hp07eDasWJ7ajBB1wIYA82MczvM_TTNe4cGnOqBdi4xNZ-RQ7mTk3d8Umq26Cux91IeWXX_lF6UXo7jaPDFMZ-t0stpK73AdIZWevH4qj2LUKp9TBRijdfvTDWK0A0Lx5CrZPfHwSKch1H1cPPI8rtW_nTR0-qfAAAA__-tH3l4) to trigger a special election that could replace Miller on the ballot in a Cleveland-area district Trump carried by 11 points.
## Women Outnumber Men in US Workforce
Women now hold [more payroll jobs than men](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2u4yAQxfGnwZ2tAYw_Copt3GXbLa0JDPHsYogAJfLbr3LvI9z-r6Ofzp_bfkOOnB6_8STbQt4TvWuk1qjsXDDVVvgfVYfJUSQfqdaTdgVq6mHpQe8eOV772HkbiBTpjqycFzMbaYzsDotSo9Nu0WqCSY1rMNN4D2rWfnaLx3vH9rMGC2gJYAwMK65yWsdlWb1GA0GMQJ5bLsPfzKkdFOKVX1QGl88u2qO1ZxX6l1CbUFvg9KEOFx45fwqhNnI55fMSasPS2EWqQm214dUf-aT-nq9QmJLvU3733zG7XiqQAKsah6OdsSvWP98cI9dpFiM8TuT4JWg_uu1l1f8AAAD__1DXgZk) in the United States for only the third time in history, and economists say this time may be permanent. Unlike past flips during the Great Recession and just before the pandemic, a former Federal Reserve economist [found this shift](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOrCAYxfGnwQ6DIAoFxW3s5rZbGoQPYQdhAmTIvP3GfYXt_tXvJOfrsT90iCGd__UFqrm8J-g1QmtQ9lB0qq2EJ1Sjk4EINkKtF-yU0AUTgQnbrQ7xs8-DVQ6AAhtATavgK584nwavllVaeSxGSDEfzlBJzTHZ1ZiZEXAAQ1C3RgRhEyGck1FqOS1yFkJapjlxaCZgQ8tl_M4hNQ8ufvIbymjyNUTlW3tVxP4huiG69d5HH0pIZ9THmMuJ6Hb7iG6E3X2Xzx33fEHCXr8Bm5grWNw84J7L0-ViAJ-QLBR86hei21CUffUQY6jLimZyXjrE3_32p9Peiv4EAAD___mggCM) is structural: two-thirds of the 1.2 million jobs added in the past two years went to women. Men are driving the change by leaving. Male labor force participation has fallen by nearly 20 percentage points since 1948, and one landmark study found that young men poured roughly three-quarters of their newfound free time into video games. Read [the study in PDF here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DtygzAQgOHTQGdGD_SgUJGGzmlTamRpZW-8gEcSJr59Jr5C-n--4v86-3NAwvX6GRZwLW9-haMStAbFYwlrbQXvUGNYIxAkgloX8IIJfWL2xKRPAenlxz65DCBA9uC4scoorhTvby6OMUvBdIrMGCszv1y4sVxYG43Wmvfo_jRmmeSMKcWGKUxcT6O1U5JBsdyNDBK2rQzfG67tBple2xPKELelJ3dr7VE7-dGJuRPzcRzDEso9XHcM76QTc0aC2omZAOtewNP-sxeEOjxS7otLjwOJsGrTjey6BKQ33f714-nEbwAAAP__rBx0uQ). The jobs themselves tell the story. Health care and social assistance added more than 680,000 positions over the past year, according to [federal data](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDvOnTAQhVdjukGDwRgKijR0f9qUaLCHixM_kO1cdHcfkSYLSHl0pPP4fnxtX-S8i6_vFHipR9oi38VzrZw3lymWmt0vLoaiYc_WcymBN4lyBJwA-82S859taOxyMEvuG146PSmtOqW65lw0aZptx7PddaftYXmYDeup19gN-zE1bnnScMK-Q1QK25nmbpyHaZptTwoPMSBbV1NufyYX68mH_6Q359ak0PjlrPUqov8m5Crket93u_vSvtJbyDVdv3ch18pWyPWpEXI9mXw9wVBmoGihJOPIA5XiSn1uAofLp0_gWMFFk5kKW9g_IGGGi7N5jJRhnFAhwpFTgEDZnCBRKqjpnxrbs4YmL_a6nfeujFoM-Ark_N_x9b-Ivxf5JwAA___GqZSY), while male-heavy sectors like manufacturing and transportation shed jobs.
